title: The general sheaf pullback unit and tensor comparisons are invertible
statement: Let C,D be categories with Grothendieck topologies J,K, and A a braided monoidal category. Suppose weak sheafification exists on both sites for A and the sheafification morphism classes are monoidal, so their sheaf tensor products are the localized presheaf tensor products. Let F:C to D be continuous, and suppose pointwise left Kan extension along F.op exists for every A-valued presheaf on C. Give its sheafified pullback the oplax structure transferred from the canonical lax pushforward under their canonical adjunction. If every CostructuredArrow F.op V is connected, the actual oplax unit map is invertible. If every such comma category is sifted and tensorLeft M preserves its colimits for every M in A, every actual oplax tensor map L(S tensor T) to LS tensor LT is invertible. These are the same sheafification and monoidal conventions as [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport].

proof.text: Reuse the existing complete generic instances. Left Kan extension sends the constant unit diagram to the unit when its comma categories are connected. It commutes with the tensor product when those categories are sifted and tensoring preserves their colimits; braiding supplies preservation on the right. Compose with the strong monoidal sheafification functor. The two composites L after source sheafification and left Kan extension after target sheafification are left adjoints to naturally isomorphic right adjoints, the underlying-presheaf restriction of the canonical pushforward. Its natural identification is monoidal. The conjugate unit and tensor comparison identities therefore identify their oplax comparisons. Invertibility for the unit descends after cancellation of the image of the source sheafification unit comparison. For tensors, first obtain invertibility on source-sheafified presheaves by cancellation; then use naturality along the counit isomorphisms sheafify(S.obj) to S and sheafify(T.obj) to T. This proves invertibility of the actual mate maps, rather than merely constructing unrelated object isomorphisms. Both generic instances are already proved in the cited source.
